claims.text: The precursor is an equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr blend containing metallic powders and TaH0.5, NbH, HfH2, TiH2, and ZrH2 powders.
The precursor powders contain dissolved oxygen impurities.
Excess metallic Ti powder can function as an in-situ oxygen getter in this alloy system.
The added Ti getter reacts with dissolved oxygen to form TiO2.
Formation of TiO2 lowers oxygen activity enough to prevent alpha-HCP nucleation.
Oxygen stabilizes alpha-HCP phases in the HfNbTaTiZr alloy.
TaH0.5 is the least stable hydride in the precursor blend.
The hydrides decompose sequentially according to their formation enthalpies.
Hydride decomposition releases hydrogen and facilitates elemental diffusion and alloying.
The sintering temperature should exceed the decomposition onset of TaH0.5 while remaining below the alloy melting point.
A sufficiently slow temperature ramp permits sequential hydride decomposition.
Rapid quenching suppresses a diffusion-controlled transformation to an equilibrium alpha-BCC plus beta-BCC structure.
Rapid quenching from the homogenization temperature traps a metastable single-phase beta-BCC structure.
The proposed process produces a refined grain size.
The proposed process produces a nearly fully dense alloy.
The quenched product will be free of alpha-HCP phases and alpha-Ti precipitates.
Sintering without sufficient getter leads to oxygen-stabilized alpha-HCP phases.
Excessive oxide inclusions can compromise final density.
Detection of alpha-HCP before quenching or failure to retain single-phase beta-BCC after quenching would falsify the proposed oxygen-scavenging and quench-retention mechanism.

contradictions.description: Adding excess Ti directly to the precursor changes the nominal Hf:Nb:Ta:Ti:Zr ratio, yet the predicted product is still described as equiatomic. No separation of the getter oxide, sacrificial external-getter arrangement, or composition correction is specified.

The intervention deliberately introduces metallic Ti powder, while the falsification rule treats appearance or persistence of alpha-Ti peaks during decomposition as evidence of failure. The design does not distinguish diffraction from the added Ti getter or original Ti feedstock from newly precipitated alpha-Ti.
